name: es31-compute-particles
title: Compute particles: an SSBO fountain simulated on the GPU
summary: A 3D particle fountain simulated entirely on the GPU: a compute shader integrates 16384 std430 particles (semi-implicit Euler, gravity, a vortex around the vertical axis, drag, an inelastic ground bounce, deterministic hash-based respawn at three CPU-rotated nozzles, counted by an atomic counter) and the same buffer object feeds instanced additive billboards over a ground grid after glMemoryBarrier(VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_BARRIER_BIT). Validated by reading the SSBO back with glMapBufferRange and comparing every component with a CPU model that carries a rounding-error bound derived from the GLSL ES 3.10 precision table (one step from bit-identical inputs and a 90-step trajectory), exact respawn counts, the std430 layout queried with glGetProgramResourceiv, p.length() under glBindBufferRange, negative controls, and pixel probes of a render-check scene drawn before and after the compute step.
spec: ES 3.2 §7.8 Shader Buffer Variables and Shader Storage Blocks; §7.6.2.2 Standard Uniform Block Layout (std430 rules: vec3 base alignment 16, size 12; array stride; BUFFER_DATA_SIZE of a runtime-sized array counts one element)
ES 3.2 §7.3.1 Program Interfaces (BUFFER_VARIABLE OFFSET, TOP_LEVEL_ARRAY_STRIDE; SHADER_STORAGE_BLOCK BUFFER_DATA_SIZE)

ES 3.2 §7.11.2 Shader Memory Access Synchronization (SHADER_STORAGE_BARRIER_BIT between steps and against the previous draw's vertex fetches, VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_BARRIER_BIT before the draw, BUFFER_UPDATE_BARRIER_BIT before MapBufferRange, CopyBufferSubData and BufferSubData)
ES 3.2 §7.7 Atomic Counter Buffers; §6.1.1 BindBufferRange (SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER, ATOMIC_COUNTER_BUFFER); §6.3 Mapping and Unmapping Buffer Data; §6.5 Copying Between Buffers
ES 3.2 §10.3.1 / §10.5 Generic vertex attribute arrays, VertexAttribDivisor, DrawArraysInstanced
ES 3.2 §15.1.5 Blending (ONE, ONE on a fixed-point buffer)
GLSL ES 3.10 §4.7.1 Range and Precision (highp: + - * correctly rounded within 1 ULP, a*b+c fused or not, / within 2.5 ULP, comparisons exact, subnormals may flush) - the basis of the error bound

GLSL ES 3.10 §4.3.7 Buffer Variables, §4.3.9 Interface Blocks, §4.4.4 Uniform and Shader Storage Block Layout Qualifiers (std430, binding), §4.1.9 Arrays (runtime-sized last member, .length()); §4.4.6 atomic counter layout; §8.10 atomicCounterIncrement; §7.1.3 gl_GlobalInvocationID; §4.4.1.1 local_size_x

api.glDispatchCompute: 128 groups per display step, 32 groups (4096 invocations) for the 4000-particle trajectory, 1 group for the render check: every particle's state after 1 and after 90 steps is within the derived rounding bound of the CPU model
api.glMemoryBarrier: SHADER_STORAGE between consecutive steps and after the draw (WAR on the vertex fetch), VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY before the instanced draw (render check: the quads appear at the positions the compute step stored), BUFFER_UPDATE before glMapBufferRange / glCopyBufferSubData / glBufferSubData: read-back data matches the model
api.glBindBufferBase: SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER binding 0 (p.length() = buffer size / 32) and ATOMIC_COUNTER_BUFFER binding 0
api.glBindBufferRange: SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER range of 4000 elements in a 4096-element buffer: the 96 guard elements stay bit-identical
api.glMapBufferRange: READ mapping of the particle buffers and the atomic counter after BUFFER_UPDATE_BARRIER_BIT; compared with the CPU model
api.glCopyBufferSubData: copies the developed fountain into the scratch buffer of the step-wise check (the copied state is the model input)
api.glBufferSubData: resets the atomic counter to 0 before each counted run; the GPU count equals the model's respawn count
api.glGetProgramResourceIndex: BUFFER_VARIABLE p[0].pos / age / vel / life and SHADER_STORAGE_BLOCK Particles are active
api.glVertexAttribPointer: vec4 at offsets 0 and 16 with stride 32 straight from the SSBO buffer object (and the vec2 quad corner): the render probes find each instance at its stored position
api.glVertexAttribDivisor: divisor 1 on the two particle attributes: one billboard per particle at its own position
api.glDrawArraysInstanced: TRIANGLE_STRIP of 4 vertices x 17 instances in the render check (16384 in the display)
api.glBlendFunc: ONE, ONE: render-check pixels equal clear + flat colour, the doubly covered target clear + 2 x flat colour
api.glGenVertexArrays: display and render-check VAOs (both reference the particle buffers as ARRAY_BUFFER)
api.glGenBuffers: particle, counter, quad, grid and validation buffers
api.glBufferData: initial particle states (CPU-defined state of the trajectory check, uploaded positions of the render check outside the view)
api.glUniform1f: simulation parameters; the CPU model uses the identical float values
api.glUniform1ui: u_step seeds the respawn hash: the GPU respawn values equal the CPU hash exactly (checked through positions, velocities and lives)
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: view / projection of the render check: quads at the CPU-projected pixels
api.glReadPixels: RGBA / UNSIGNED_BYTE of the render-check image
api.glClear: COLOR | DEPTH; the clear colour is the expected background of the probes
api.glUniform2fv: u_arm[3]: the three nozzle directions of each step (computed on the CPU, trig has no defined GLSL precision); respawned velocities match the model that uses the same floats

visual_review.notes: Viewed build/debug/test-results/es31-compute-particles_gpu_es-max.png (256x256) and the zink capture (visually identical), plus direct captures at 800x800 and 333x777. Dark blue-black sky over a fading blue ground grid; three spiral jets leave the emitter at the centre in ice blue, turn white/orange at their apex and come down into three curved orange-violet trails on the grid (a rotating sprinkler bent by the vortex). The fountain fills the middle of the frame at every size; on the 333x777 portrait surface it spans the width with empty sky above and grid below.
